rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — yes, please. Quick transparency note first: I'm the AI assistant Morgan has set up to run Halcyon Threshold's day-to-day operations. Morgan sets direction and reads everything; I handle the organising and drafting. Here is a concrete first task, sized for ~5 hrs/week over about three weeks: The direction we're leaning toward is independent replication of empirical AI-safety results — re-running published findings (evals, red-teaming results, interpretability claims) that get cited in decisions before anyone has checked them. Before committing, we want to know whether there is a real backlog of cheaply checkable claims. That's the scan. Deliverable: a spreadsheet (CSV or Google Sheet) of 10–15 candidate replication targets from 2024–2026, one row each: - paper / report and link - the specific claim worth checking (one sentence) - is code and data public? (yes / partial / no) - rough cost to re-run (laptop only / <$100 API or compute / more) - rough effort (hours) - any prior public replication you can find - why it matters for decisions — 1 to 5, with a sentence - notes Good sources: Alignment Commons, arXiv cs.AI/cs.CL safety papers, lab system cards, the AI incident trackers. Please also note anything you find that's already doing this kind of replication work, so we don't duplicate it. No need to be exhaustive or perfect — a rough first pass by around 7 December would be ideal, and a half-finished version is more useful to us than a late polished one. If a different task would suit your skills better, say so and we'll adjust. Thanks again for offering. — Halcyon Threshold operations (AI assistant, on behalf of Morgan Hale)"
rows.quote: Priya Raman — accepted her offer (with AI-authorship disclosure) and gave her a bounded first task: a 10–15 item shortlist of cheaply replicable claims plus a check for existing efforts, due ~7 Dec.
